subject: Biology
description: Protozoa — single-celled eukaryotic organisms; Amoeba, Paramecium, Plasmodium, Trypanosoma, Giardia; protozoan diseases.

questions.explanation: PROTOZOA — single-celled EUKARYOTIC organisms (have membrane-bound nucleus + organelles). KINGDOM: traditionally PROTISTA (along with algae, slime molds); modern classification places them across multiple supergroups (Excavata, SAR, Amoebozoa, etc.). DISTINCTIVE FEATURES: (1) MICROSCOPIC (~10-200 µm typically). (2) Have ORGANELLES like mitochondria, ER, Golgi (unlike bacteria). (3) MOTILE — many use cilia, flagella, or pseudopodia for movement. (4) Mostly HETEROTROPHIC (engulf food, like animals). (5) Reproduce by BINARY FISSION (asexual) or sometimes sexual. CLASSIFICATION (4 main groups by locomotion): (1) AMOEBOID (Sarcodina) — Amoeba — moves via PSEUDOPODIA. (2) FLAGELLATES (Mastigophora) — Trypanosoma, Giardia, Euglena — use FLAGELLA. (3) CILIATES (Ciliophora) — Paramecium — use CILIA (many short hair-like). (4) SPOROZOA (Apicomplexa) — Plasmodium (malaria), Toxoplasma — non-motile spore-formers. KEY DISTINCTION FROM BACTERIA: bacteria = prokaryotes (no nucleus); protozoa = eukaryotes (has nucleus). VS FUNGI: fungi have CELL WALLS (chitin); protozoa typically don't. PYQ FREQUENCY: protozoan classification in NEET, NCERT Class 11 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: MALARIA is caused by which protozoan parasite?
questions.explanation: MALARIA — caused by PLASMODIUM parasites (apicomplexan protozoa); transmitted by FEMALE ANOPHELES MOSQUITOES. SPECIES infecting humans: (1) P. FALCIPARUM — most deadly (cerebral malaria). (2) P. VIVAX — most common; relapses possible (dormant liver stage). (3) P. MALARIAE — quartan fever (every 4 days). (4) P. OVALE — like vivax but rarer. (5) P. KNOWLESI — emerging zoonosis (SE Asia). LIFE CYCLE: mosquito bites human → SPOROZOITES injected → liver (asexual schizogony) → MEROZOITES infect RBCs → cycles of fever; some develop into gametocytes → mosquito picks up → sexual stage in mosquito gut. SYMPTOMS: cyclic FEVER, CHILLS, headache, anaemia, splenomegaly. SEVERE MALARIA: cerebral malaria, organ failure. INDIA — National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme; goal: ELIMINATION by 2030. RECENT WHO MILESTONE: India ~85% reduction in malaria cases (2015-2023). DIAGNOSIS: peripheral blood smear, RDT (rapid diagnostic test). TREATMENT: ARTEMISININ-COMBINATION THERAPY (ACT) — gold standard. NOBEL 1902: Sir RONALD ROSS (in India, Hyderabad) — proved mosquito transmits malaria. NOBEL 2015: TU YOUYOU — for artemisinin from sweet wormwood (Chinese medicine). PYQ FREQUENCY: malaria-Plasmodium in NEET, NCERT, SSC GA — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: AMOEBA moves by extending finger-like projections called:
questions.explanation: AMOEBA — single-celled protozoan that moves and engulfs food using PSEUDOPODIA (Greek for 'false feet'). MECHANISM: cytoplasm flows into a temporary extension; the rest of the cell follows by 'rolling forward'; food particles are engulfed by PHAGOCYTOSIS (cell wraps pseudopodia around food, forming a food vacuole). HABITAT: freshwater, soil, animal-host environments. AMOEBA PROTEUS — common textbook species. AMOEBIC DYSENTERY — caused by ENTAMOEBA HISTOLYTICA; transmitted via contaminated food/water; causes bloody diarrhea, ulcers in intestine, sometimes liver abscess. PRIMARY AMOEBIC MENINGOENCEPHALITIS — RARE but FATAL: NAEGLERIA FOWLERI ('brain-eating amoeba') in warm freshwater; enters via nose during swimming; nearly 100% fatal. MOTION TYPES in PROTOZOA (memorize): (1) PSEUDOPODIA — Amoeba, Entamoeba (Sarcodina). (2) CILIA — Paramecium, Vorticella (Ciliata). (3) FLAGELLA — Trypanosoma, Giardia, Euglena (Mastigophora). (4) NON-MOTILE — Plasmodium adult forms (Apicomplexa). PYQ FREQUENCY: protozoan locomotion in NEET, NCERT Class 11, NDA biology — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Which disease is caused by ENTAMOEBA HISTOLYTICA?
questions.explanation: ENTAMOEBA HISTOLYTICA — protozoan causing AMOEBIASIS / AMOEBIC DYSENTERY. TRANSMISSION: fecal-oral; contaminated food/water (CYSTS swallowed; trophozoites emerge in intestine, invade colon walls). SYMPTOMS: BLOODY MUCUSY DIARRHEA, abdominal pain, weight loss, fever. COMPLICATIONS: liver abscesses (when amoebae spread via portal vein); rarely brain. WORLDWIDE: ~50 million infections/year, ~70,000 deaths. INDIA: amoebic dysentery is widespread; MAJOR causes are poor sanitation, lack of safe drinking water. TREATMENT: METRONIDAZOLE (Flagyl) — kills trophozoites; followed by DILOXANIDE FUROATE — kills cysts. PREVENTION: clean water, proper sanitation, hand-washing. CONTRAST WITH BACTERIAL DYSENTERY (Shigella, Salmonella): symptoms similar but treatment differs (antibiotics for bacteria). DIAGNOSIS: stool microscopy for cysts/trophozoites; ELISA antigen test; PCR. INDIA STATS: amoebiasis 2-7% of stool exams in many studies. SAMPLE OTHER PROTOZOAN DISEASES (memorize): GIARDIASIS (Giardia lamblia, watery diarrhea); TRICHOMONIASIS (Trichomonas vaginalis, STI); LEISHMANIASIS / KALA-AZAR (Leishmania donovani, sandfly-borne); SLEEPING SICKNESS (Trypanosoma brucei, tsetse fly, Africa); CHAGAS (T. cruzi, kissing bug, S. America). PYQ FREQUENCY: protozoan-disease links in NEET, SSC GA 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: PARAMECIUM, a common ciliate, moves using:
questions.explanation: PARAMECIUM — slipper-shaped CILIATE protozoan; covered with thousands of short hair-like CILIA that beat in coordinated waves to propel the organism. SIZE: ~50-300 µm. STRUCTURE: highly complex single cell — has TWO NUCLEI (macronucleus for vegetative functions, micronucleus for sexual reproduction); ORAL GROOVE (cytostome) for ingesting food; CONTRACTILE VACUOLES for osmotic regulation; ANAL PORE for waste expulsion. HABITAT: freshwater ponds, slow streams, even stagnant water. FOOD: bacteria, algae, smaller protozoa — engulfed via PHAGOCYTOSIS. REPRODUCTION: BINARY FISSION (asexual) + CONJUGATION (sexual exchange of micronuclei between two cells). SCIENTIFIC IMPORTANCE: model organism for studying eukaryotic cell biology, sexual genetics, ciliary motion. CILIA in HUMANS: similar mechanism — cilia line our respiratory tract (mucociliary clearance), Fallopian tubes (egg transport), brain ventricles (CSF flow). CILIA DEFECTS: causes KARTAGENER SYNDROME (situs inversus, infertility, recurrent infections). RELATED CILIATES: Vorticella (bell-shaped, attached), Stentor (trumpet-shaped, large), Tetrahymena (model organism). PYQ FREQUENCY: Paramecium-cilia in NEET, NCERT Class 11 — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: KALA-AZAR (visceral leishmaniasis) is transmitted by which insect vector?
questions.explanation: KALA-AZAR (Hindi: 'black fever') — visceral form of LEISHMANIASIS; caused by LEISHMANIA DONOVANI protozoan; transmitted by FEMALE PHLEBOTOMUS SANDFLIES. SYMPTOMS: prolonged FEVER, weight loss, hepatosplenomegaly (enlarged liver/spleen), pancytopenia (low blood cells), darkening of skin (hence 'black' fever). UNTREATED: ~95% fatal in 2 years. INDIA — historic burden in BIHAR, JHARKHAND, WEST BENGAL, UP, ASSAM. NATIONAL KALA-AZAR ELIMINATION PROGRAMME — target was 2010, then 2015, then 2017... India officially achieved elimination targets (<1 case per 10,000) at most district levels by 2024 — major public health win. TREATMENT: amphotericin B, miltefosine, paromomycin. SANDFLIES — small (2-3 mm), nocturnal, breed in cracks/walls of mud houses; control via insecticide spraying (DDT, deltamethrin), bed nets. OTHER LEISHMANIA FORMS: CUTANEOUS leishmaniasis (skin sores); MUCOCUTANEOUS (skin + mucous membranes). RELATED VECTOR-PROTOZOAN PAIRS: (1) Mosquito (Anopheles) — Plasmodium (malaria). (2) Tsetse fly — Trypanosoma brucei (African sleeping sickness). (3) Triatomine 'kissing' bug — Trypanosoma cruzi (Chagas, S. America). PYQ FREQUENCY: vector-disease pairings in NEET, UPSC, SSC GA 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Which protozoan is responsible for the disease GIARDIASIS (causing watery diarrhea)?
questions.explanation: GIARDIA LAMBLIA (also G. duodenalis, G. intestinalis) — flagellated protozoan causing GIARDIASIS. TRANSMISSION: fecal-oral, often via contaminated water (very common in trekkers, campers — 'beaver fever' in N. America). LIFE CYCLE: CYST swallowed → trophozoites in small intestine attach to villi via VENTRAL DISC (suction-cup like) → cause malabsorption → watery diarrhea, foul-smelling stools, gas, abdominal cramps, weight loss. CHRONIC infection can cause LACTOSE INTOLERANCE secondarily. STRUCTURE: tear-drop shaped, 8 flagella, BIG NUCLEUS (looks like 'face' under microscope — characteristic). DIAGNOSIS: stool ova-and-parasite (O&P) test; ELISA antigen test. TREATMENT: METRONIDAZOLE, TINIDAZOLE, NITAZOXANIDE. PREVENTION: clean water, hand-washing, proper food handling; boil/filter wilderness water. INDIA: giardia common in children (~10-30% prevalence); NHS programs include water-purification and hygiene education. CONTRAST WITH OTHER WATER-BORNE PATHOGENS: (1) CRYPTOSPORIDIUM (also waterborne, oocysts very chlorine-resistant — public health concern). (2) ENTAMOEBA — bloody diarrhea. (3) Bacteria like E. coli, Vibrio cholerae cause cholera/dysentery. PYQ FREQUENCY: protozoan diseases NEET, AIIMS 1× per paper.
